plan.summary: This 4-week block starts a 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one focused S&C session each week. Week 1 establishes a simple baseline on a main lower-body strength pattern, then Weeks 2-4 build general power, strength, trunk stiffness, and upper-body support with bodyweight-only work that fits a beginner and stays recoverable alongside boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general strength, jumping power, trunk stiffness, and upper-body support with simple bodyweight work done fast and clean.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress harder unilateral strength and sharper explosive work while keeping the weekly dose easy to recover from around boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength with a small dose and emphasize faster, sharper jumps, throws, and strike-supportive speed qualities.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can on every rep. Reset between reps and land softly in a stable stance.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is tight. Start from a still quarter squat and jump fast.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable box if landing mechanics are better there. Step down each rep.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with easy practice sets, then work up to your hardest clean set of 4-6 reps per side. Log the reps completed and how solid they felt. This sets a baseline for future progression on your main lower-body strength pattern.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up gradually with a few easy sets, then perform one hardest clean set of 4-6 reps per side using strict control and full range. Log the variation and reps so future work can progress from this baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your hardest clean set per side and aim to improve control or reps next time.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot elevation is awkward. Stay tall and control the bottom.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a knee-height or lower step if split squats bother the hips or knees.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Keep a straight line from head to heel and stop 1-2 reps before form breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, box, or table if floor reps are not yet clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lower if regular push-ups are too easy but you have no load.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Pull the chest to the bar or edge, keep the body rigid, and pause briefly at the top.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a sturdy table if no low bar is available. Move under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if the anchor is very secure. Keep reps smooth and controlled.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Press the lower back into the floor and keep ribs down the whole set.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot keep the lower back flat in the hollow hold.

substitutionOptions.name: Tuck Hollow Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Bend the knees and shorten the lever if full position is too hard.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Keep the body in one straight line and do not let the hips sag.

substitutionOptions.name: Short-Lever Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Bend the knees if the full side plank is too demanding.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump with max intent and full reset between reps. Stop if jump height clearly drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler jump with less countermovement.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable box and focus on crisp takeoff and quiet landing.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use smooth full-range reps and leave 2 reps in reserve on each set.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your strongest clean set of 6 per side and progress with better depth, balance, or a harder variation.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if balance limits the rear-foot-elevated version.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats irritate the knees.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Move under control, lock in the trunk, and stop with 1-2 clean reps left.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Raise the hands if you cannot keep clean reps for the full range.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Slow the lowering phase to make the set harder without losing position.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Start from a dead stop each rep if possible and keep shoulders away from the ears.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Good option if a bar is not available.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Only use with a very secure setup.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Drive through the whole foot, finish with the glute, and avoid arching the lower back.

substitutionOptions.name: Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use both legs if the single-leg version cramps or loses pelvic control.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep the chin tucked slightly and do not let the lower back peel off the floor.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot keep the trunk position clean.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Every rep should be fast and snappy. Rest enough to keep quality high.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want an even simpler jump pattern.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Keep the box low enough that landing stays athletic, not tucked.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Own the bottom position and keep 1-2 reps in reserve. If bodyweight is too easy, slow the lowering phase to 3 seconds.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your strongest controlled set of 8 per side and try to improve quality before adding difficulty.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Good fallback if balance or setup becomes the limiter.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you need a more knee-friendly single-leg strength option.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Press fast on the way up but keep the body rigid. Stop before the hips sag or the head reaches first.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you still need a simpler version for clean reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are easy and you need more challenge.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Keep elbows and wrists quiet, squeeze the upper back, and lower under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Simple substitute if a bar is unavailable.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Only use with a secure anchor and enough space to lean back safely.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Step back softly, keep front foot flat, and drive up with balance and control.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if stepping back feels awkward.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if lunges irritate the knees.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Push the floor away and keep the top hip stacked over the bottom hip.

substitutionOptions.name: Short-Lever Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use bent knees if the full position cannot be held cleanly.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Keep reps sharp and stop well before any drop in height or stiffness.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a very simple crisp jump option.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low box and focus on clean takeoff and landing.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Deload week. Keep the movement clean and controlled with about 2-3 reps left in reserve.

performanceTarget.prompt: Use this week to move well and note whether the reps feel easier than Week 2.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a simpler deload option with the same pattern.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you need a lower-fatigue single-leg option.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave plenty in the tank and keep every rep identical.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this to make the deload easier while keeping good speed.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Smooth reps only. Pause briefly at the top and keep the body braced.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Good simple substitute if needed.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Move smoothly and finish each rep with the glute, not the lower back.

substitutionOptions.name: Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use both legs if you want a lighter recovery option.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep the trunk tight and stop before the lower back loses contact with the floor.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow hold is still too demanding.
